statement.text:
Suppose that G is a one-relator group containing non-trivial elements of finite
order and N is a subgroup of G generated by all elements of finite order. Is it true
that any subgroup of G that intersects N trivially is a free group? One can show that
the answer is affirmative in the cases where G/N has non-trivial centre or satisfies a
non-trivial identity.                                               D. I. Moldavanskiı̆
